inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.

requested_area.areaDesc: Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

fields.description: NCM alert: convective clouds may bring light to moderate rain, heavy at times, to some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior. In effect Saturday 13:30 to 21:00.
fields.headline: NCM alert: possible rain, heavy at times, Saturday 13:30 to 21:00
fields.instruction: Take care if you are outdoors or driving while it rains. Follow official updates at https://alerts.example.ae.
fields.note_for_reviewer: The source gives no specific protective actions, so the instruction is generic. The source also gives times without a time zone (assumed local) and names only 'Saturday'; the WAM article date of 2026-08-22 is a Saturday.

versions.description: تنبيه من NCM: قد تجلب السحب الركامية أمطارًا خفيفة إلى متوسطة، غزيرة أحيانًا، على بعض المناطق الشرقية والجنوبية والغربية وأجزاء من المناطق الداخلية. ساري المفعول يوم السبت من 13:30 إلى 21:00.
versions.headline: تنبيه من NCM: احتمال هطول أمطار، غزيرة أحيانًا، يوم السبت من 13:30 إلى 21:00

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin. It gives the same hazard (convective cloud with light to moderate rain, heavy at times), the same window (Saturday 13:30 to 21:00), and the same areas (some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior). Severity Moderate and certainty Possible are consistent with the bulletin's wording ("possibility", "may become heavy") and the CAP definitions. The alert contains no unverified report.

no_basis.concern: The register entry is a demo authority and not a real issuer, and the WMO register lists no authorization basis for the UAE. This is a verification question for people, not a defect in the alert.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE issuer register or authorization basis for the sending entity

queries: CAP 1.2 sender authorization issuer register status Actual Exercise
CAP msgType Update Cancel references correction original alert
UAE early warning authority issuing alerts area NCM
payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with all areas and categories. The alert's area matches the requested area drawn for event uae-rain-2026-08-22. The context is a real event and the status is Actual, so there is no drill mismatch. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach and no earlier alerts. The msgType is Alert, so no references are needed.

no_basis.concern: The TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, while both languages run to several pages. This conflicts with the multi-page note, and the handset spec states it sets no page limit.
no_basis.searched_for: TDRA cell broadcast handset specification page limit; 3GPP TS 23.041 pages maximum 15

no_basis.concern: The first page of each language carries the hazard but no explicit protective action. The text only gives the effect period, with no instruction to the public.
no_basis.searched_for: cell broadcast first page hazard and action

queries: TDRA cell broadcast handset specification Arabic English
3GPP TS 23.041 cell broadcast pages UCS-2 maximum 15
cell broadcast first page hazard and action
payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 2 pages in GSM-7 and Arabic is 5 pages in UCS-2, both well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. The encodings suit each script. The first page of each language opens with the NCM alert and the hazard (rain from convective clouds). Length is a recorded gap (G6) and is not re-raised. The TS040 summary's 1-page limit is a possible conflict, but the handset spec shown sets no page limit and the gap is already reported.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic was machine translated and has no human review recorded. Machine translation is a general risk for the protective action, but the text I compared is faithful.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE requirement on human review of machine-translated Arabic in public alerts

no_basis.concern: The abbreviation NCM is left in Latin script in the Arabic rather than being written as the Arabic name of the National Center of Meteorology. This is a stylistic point, not a difference in meaning.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE rule on how the issuing authority's name is written in Arabic alert text
